changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.43[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Usenet playback[/COLOR]
-Smoother playback of heavy releases (4K remux, long extended cuts). Tested with a 157 GB 4K remux on an NVIDIA Shield and on a tablet: no more buffering while watching, and the short stalls after a seek or a resume went from about 16-18 seconds in total to 2-3.
-New: heavy films get more Easynews connections on their own. Each connection gives about 5-6 Mbit/s, so for a film averaging 85 Mbit/s the engine raises its ceiling to 28, and adds 8 more each minute it still falls short, up to 40 (Easynews allows 60 per account; 8 stay for the health check). Lighter films and the connections setting are left as they are, and it stops as soon as Easynews refuses more.
-While a film plays, or stays paused less than 10 minutes, every Easynews connection stays open, so a seek or a resume finds them ready. After a long pause the ones the film needed reopen all at once.
-A stuck article is asked for again on a second connection only when it is slow compared with the others. When every article is slow the line is full, and a second copy only took room from the ones that were needed.
-The engine decodes each article about 30% faster with the very same bytes, copies it once instead of twice, and asks for the whole read-ahead in one go: 20-30% less processor in tests.
-While a film plays from Usenet, luc_kodi's background work (Trakt, SIMKL and watched-mark syncs, the update check, the precache and Catalog Update, the sync between paired devices) waits until it ends instead of competing with the engine.
-Tip: for 4K remuxes set Kodi's Settings > Services > Caching to Memory size 128 MB (256 MB on devices with plenty of RAM), Read factor Adaptive and Chunk size 512 KB. Kodi splits that memory in two for video, so 128 MB keeps about 48 MB ahead.
[COLOR fffdb515]Under the hood[/COLOR]
-During Usenet playback kodi.log gets one line a minute: the speed coming from Easynews against what the film needs (with the real length read from the MKV, as an extended cut can run an hour longer than the cinema runtime), connections in use, seconds of film ready ahead and second copies skipped.
